pill.desc: clear to very opalescent, colorless to pale yellow solution in a single-dose vial

tell: A humanized antibody with a terminal half-life of 5 to 7 days, also available as a weekly subcutaneous autoinjector.

clues.text: Degraded by proteolytic enzymes, and not expected to undergo renal elimination or hepatic metabolism. Absolute bioavailability is about 77.5% after 500 mg and 53% after 360 mg subcutaneously.
A recombinant humanized protein expressed in a Chinese hamster ovary cell line, with an approximate molecular weight of 150 kDa.
Approved under a BLA in 200 mg/2 mL and 500 mg/5 mL single-dose vials, and in autoinjectors. Dosing is once every 2 weeks by infusion or once a week by injection.

Boxed warning for ARIA, brain-imaging abnormalities with swelling or microbleeds, which can be fatal. Contraindicated in serious hypersensitivity; infusion reactions and microhemorrhages most often stop treatment.
Alzheimer's disease, started in patients with mild cognitive impairment or mild dementia.
Directed against aggregated soluble and insoluble forms of amyloid beta, and reduces amyloid beta plaques.
The generic name begins with L and has nine letters.
